quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Where should a load be placed on a motorcycle?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them in saddlebags. Placing loads high or against the back rest raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and affects balance. Always distribute weight equally on both sides.

questions.question: To prevent fatigue on a long ride, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Limit the distance traveled in a day.

questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from wind and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day and take a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants because you will feel very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Ride more slowly than you would normally.
Start slowing earlier than you would normally.
Not communicate with the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not communicate with the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, so the motorcycle responds more slowly. Ride slower, brake earlier, and keep more distance behind other vehicles. Always warn your passenger about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane in traffic, you should:

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Flash your lights to scare the animal.

questions.explanation: Stay in your lane in traffic. Swerving to avoid a small animal could cause you to crash into another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting another car.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, a group of motorcyclists should:
questions.explanation: Use a single-file formation when riding through curves, taking turns, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Riding on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be seen easily.
Is not recommended because drivers seldom use their side mirrors and may not see you.
Is recommended because a passenger may tell the driver you are there.
Is illegal because you must ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because drivers seldom use their side mirrors and may not see you.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. Ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: When entering a turn, a rider should:

options.text: Move their shoulders to match the angle of the turn.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.explanation: Reduce your speed before turning. Close the throttle and use both brakes if needed.

questions.question: When riding in fog, you should:

options.text: Alternate between the low and high beams.

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. Do not use high beams around other vehicles.

questions.question: If taking a long trip, you should:

options.text: Try to minimize the number of rest breaks.
Use artificial stimulants, like caffeine, if you feel drowsy.
Dress warmly to avoid getting too cold during the ride.
Schedule more than 12 hours of riding a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to avoid getting too cold during the ride.
questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day and take breaks at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants because extreme fatigue follows when they wear off.

questions.question: When turning left, you should:

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time.

questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn to make the motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use the brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes together whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What guarantees that another driver sees you?
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that another driver sees you. Always assume that any vehicle could enter your path.

questions.question: A rectangular sign can be:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering or symbols. Riders must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: In normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance when riding?
questions.explanation: Keep at least four seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead in normal conditions. Increase this distance when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Before a passenger rides, you should instruct them to do everything except:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has started.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Keep a large space between themselves and you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a large space between themselves and you.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to mount the motorcycle only after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as they can without crowding you and hold onto the handholds or your waist. Keep legs away from hot and moving parts.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles at speeds under 30 mph.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate when riding in groups. This signal means "follow me."

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Helps protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Should be avoided because it can cause heat-related problems.
Should only be worn if it is a light color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants in hot weather. They protect you from crashes and also help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.

questions.question: When riding in rain or fog, you should:

options.text: Switch between low and high beam settings.

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in snow, rain, or fog. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: When the lead rider raises their left arm and points with one finger, what does it mean?
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. This signal tells riders to move into a single-file line.

questions.question: If you need to brake while turning a curve, you should:

options.text: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
Brake as hard as you would on a straight road.
Wait until you finish the curve before braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip when a motorcycle leans than when it sits upright. Try to straighten your motorcycle before braking. If you must brake in a curve, apply the brakes slowly and gently.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without one.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries during a crash than riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, it should have all of the following qualities, except:

options.text: Meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards. It should fit snugly all around and have no damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Push the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
Push the handle grip away from the direction you want to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve and avoid a hazard, push the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, push the left handle grip, then push the right to straighten. To swerve right, push the right handle grip, then the left.

questions.question: When loading items on a motorcycle:

options.text: Put heavier items toward the front.
Put heavier items toward the back.
Mount loads behind the rear axle.
Put lighter items in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items toward the front.
questions.explanation: Place loads forward with heavier items at the front. Keep all loads over or in front of the rear axle. Pack lighter items behind you.

questions.question: Under normal riding conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance behind other vehicles in normal conditions. Increase this distance if conditions are poor.

questions.question: Riding in cold weather for long periods can cause all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Long rides in cold weather can cause severe chills, tiredness, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from cold weather.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time to hazards, you should:

options.text: Always ride below the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In risky areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and both brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to danger.

questions.question: Who should set the pace for a group of riders?

options.text: The riders right behind the leader

questions.explanation: The last rider in a group should set the pace. This makes sure no riders get left behind.

questions.question: Proper riding clothes provide all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Good riding clothes protect you from injury in a crash and from weather problems like hot or cold temperatures.

questions.question: Swerving a motorcycle requires:

options.text: You should do it to avoid a hazard on a slippery road.

questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick move that needs a lot of traction to do safely. Avoid making sudden moves like swerving on slippery roads.

questions.question: When riding in traffic, a motorcycle operator should:

options.text: Always ride in the same part of the lane.
Change their lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride in the left part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change their lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position based on the road and traffic around you.

questions.question: If you carry a load in a sidecar, the motorcycle's stopping distance:

options.text: Will be the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Adding weight increases the motorcycle's inertia, which may increase stopping distance. Start slowing down earlier when carrying a load or passenger in a sidecar.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: To be seen better at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Reduce your distance from other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on to help other drivers see you. Stay in a lane position where others can see you easily. Keep your distance from other vehicles so you can avoid them if needed. Do not assume a driver sees you, even if you make eye contact.

questions.question: When riding at night, maintain a minimum following distance of:
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see and judge distance. Keep at least three seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. You may need more time to see when the vehicle stops and to brake.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn both your head and your shoulders.
Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Move only your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn just your head and keep your eyes level.

questions.question: When being passed, do not move to the far side of your lane because it:

options.text: Stops the passing driver from returning too early.
May cause the passing driver to return too early.
Encourages the passing driver to finish quickly.
Encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: May cause the passing driver to return too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane may tempt the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: When being passed, do not move to the far side of your lane because:

options.text: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too early.
You may block another vehicle from passing you.
The side closest to the passing vehicle is better.
You may feel a stronger wind blast on the far side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Do not ride on the far side of your lane when being passed. This may tempt the driver to return to your lane before there is enough room to do so safely.

questions.question: The front brake supplies about how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake and provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while in a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Apply both brakes suddenly while leaning.

questions.explanation: If you must stop quickly in a curve, straighten your motorcycle first, then apply the brakes. If you cannot straighten up, apply the brakes smoothly and slowly. Reduce your lean angle and increase brake pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: Applies some rear braking when you use the front brake.
Applies some front braking when you use the rear brake.
Applies equal braking to both the front and rear when either brake is used.
Remembers how hard you usually brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies some front braking when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system applies some front braking whenever you use the rear brake. Check your owner's manual to learn more about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the rear of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders behind them can watch and help them.

questions.question: When another motorcycle passes you from behind, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: Stay on the left side of your lane.
Stay in the center of your lane.
Stay on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: The center of your lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may cause the other rider to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: What can increase fatigue while riding?

options.text: Starting to ride late in the day.

questions.explanation: Protect yourself against tiring conditions like wind and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day. Stop for a break at least every two hours. Do not take stimulants, as you may feel very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: What may need to be adjusted to carry a passenger?
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. You may need to adjust the shocks. You should also adjust the headlight and mirrors because the motorcycle will sit at a different angle.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes if you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: How do motorcycle headlights compare to car headlights?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are generally smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: For people under 21, what is the lowest blood alcohol content (BAC) that is illegal to have while driving?
questions.explanation: In New Jersey, people under 21 cannot operate a motor vehicle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of 0.01 percent or higher.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a cause of motorcycle wobble?
questions.explanation: Wobbles usually come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not try to speed up to stop a wobble.
